messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: p99 streaming latency breach detected on /v1/stream (SLO 3s). Current p95=2.1s p99=9.8s. Increased error rate and timeouts observed. Auto-paging oncall. :rotating_light:
Maya (oncall): ack — I'm on it. tagging @Raj for infra help, @Emily for routing/fallbacks. what's the customer impact? :eyes:
Raj: seeing tail stalls on a subset of streaming workers. throughput OK but tail latency shoots up when requests hit node-gpu-23. investigating hardware metrics now.
Emily: routing shows ~7% of streaming traffic going to dedicated-pool-legacy that contains node-gpu-23. Can we divert that pool while we triage?
Maya (oncall): yes — plan: 1) divert traffic off node-gpu-23 to fallback pool, 2) cordon+drain node-gpu-23, 3) collect nvidia diagnostics and logs, 4) if ECC/thermal found, do live-evacuate and mark node for reprobe.
Alejandro: running remote checks. quick health dump:
```
# tail -n 80 /var/log/redwood/serving/node-gpu-23.log
[13:21:01] kv-cache: miss spike
[13:21:04] runtime: stream stall detected, kv-evict triggered
[13:21:18] hw: ECC correctable errors rising on GPU0
[13:21:22] hw: thermal throttle event on GPU0
[13:21:30] runtime: request timeout 30s
```
Raj: confirmed — nvlink errors + correctable ECC counts climbing. sample output from node:
```
$ nvidia-smi --query-ecc=single_bit_errors,volatile_double_bit_errors --format=csv
single_bit_errors_gpu0, volatile_double_bit_errors_gpu0
142, 0
```
Looks like a flakey DIMM/GPU causing ECC bursts and thermal spikes.
Maya (oncall): opsbot, can you apply a quick routing override to stop sending new streams to that pool? fallback to dedup-stream-pool-2 that has spare capacity.
opsbot: @Maya routing-change accepted. RuleId=rt-2026-0315-01. Shifted 9.2% of streaming traffic away from dedicated-pool-legacy -> dedup-stream-pool-2. :white_check_mark:
Emily: starting canary for fallback to quantized-variant-q4 on dedup-stream-pool-2 for 10% of traffic to reduce memory pressure and latency. Monitoring for quality regressions.
Maya (oncall): Raj — please cordon/drain node-gpu-23 and remove it from the pooling. Keep it powered for diagnostics. Command you can run:
```
kubectl cordon node-gpu-23
kubectl drain node-gpu-23 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=10m
```
Raj: executing now. draining pods. some long-running KV sessions — using graceful eviction with 3 minute timeout.
platform-runbook-bot: NOTE: For thermal/ECC swelling on G5X nodes, follow runbook 'gpu-ecc-thermal-live' -> step 2b (collect ecc counters, fan curve, and attach syslog).
Raj: attached ECC counters and dmesg excerpt to the node ticket (#NODE-523). excerpt:
```
[13:22:11] Correctable ECC error on GPU0: addr=0x7ff... count=1
[13:22:12] thermal_zone0: cooling_device=fan0 triggered
[13:22:13] Correctable ECC error on GPU0: addr=0x7fe... count=2
```
Alejandro: Also saw GPU clock downscaling events in the kernel. suspect thermal or firmware fallback kicking in — that will spike latency for streaming because KV cache hits are delayed.
Maya (oncall): Customer impact: initial alert correlates to elevated tail latency for streaming sessions for ~7% of customers using high-throughput endpoints. Errors returned as streaming stall/timeouts; estimated 3% increase in 5xx across affected tenant set. Not a full outage but SLO breach for p99. Escalate to support for customer notifications?
Emily: Support (cc: cs-notify) — please prep a short message: "We are investigating elevated streaming latency; some requests may see delays. We're routing traffic away from affected hardware and expect mitigation within ~20–30 minutes."
Alejandro: while drain finishes, I'm going to attempt a firmware reset on GPU0 via management interface (out-of-band) — if that clears ECC counters it might be transient. I'll coordinate with Raj.
Raj: drain completed. node-gpu-23 pods evacuated. performing soft-reset per runbook: `nvswitch --reset` then watch ECC counters for 5 minutes.
Alejandro: performed reset. ECC counters not decreasing immediately; performing power-cycle now (scheduled 2 min to complete).
Maya (oncall): monitoring p95/p99 now. current p95=1.9s p99=3.4s — improving but still above target. Streaming error rate down from +3% to +0.7%. good trend.
opsbot: routing-change: additional 2.5% traffic shifted away from legacy pool to spare capacity.
platform-runbook-bot: If correctable ECC count continues to climb after power-cycle, escalate hardware team and tag node for warranty replacement.
Alejandro: post-power-cycle ECC counters reset to baseline, thermal events stop in syslog. kernel logs show GPU clock restored. Looks like transient hardware glitch, probable cooling spike.
Maya (oncall): With node out of pool and traffic diverted, p99 back to 1.6s. Reverting temporary quantized fallback after monitoring window.
Emily: rolling back the quantized-variant canary — quality checks passed, no customer-visible regressions.
Maya (oncall): Summary for now: root cause: transient ECC/thermal spike on node-gpu-23 causing GPU throttling and KV cache stalls, leading to p99 tail spike for streaming. Mitigation: divert traffic, drain and soft-reset+power-cycle node, temporarily route to dedup-stream-pool-2 and canary quantized variant. Customer impact: brief p99 SLO breach, ~7% of streaming traffic affected, small uptick in 5xx (~3%) for affected tenants, now resolved.
Maya (oncall): next steps: hardware team to monitor node for 24h, schedule physical inspection if ECC reappears; add automated alert for ECC correctable error rate > 10/min; add telemetry to tie per-node thermal events to SLO spikes for faster correlation.
incident-bot: INCIDENT: resolved (auto). duration: ~32m. link: /incidents/6170002468.
Alejandro: filing hardware ticket with datacenter ops (#HW-998) and marking node for postmortem.
Raj: putting a short runbook note under "gpu-thermal-ecc" about checking nv-host-fan profiles — saw fan curve not ramping quickly enough.
Maya (oncall): thanks team. I'll draft a one-paragraph customer-facing blurb for CS and a short internal postmortem. :white_check_mark:
